headline: Massachusetts nominates 104 Opportunity Zones across 46 municipalities
dek: The proposed federal tax-incentive areas would take effect in 2027, but Treasury certification and private investment decisions are still ahead.
body: Massachusetts has nominated 104 census tracts in 46 municipalities for the next round of federal Opportunity Zone designations, opening a new phase in the state’s effort to steer private investment toward neighborhoods with housing, business and infrastructure needs. The Healey-Driscoll administration submitted the nominations to the U.S. Department of the Treasury on Oct. 2, according to the [state’s 2026 Opportunity Zone program page](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/2026-massachusetts-opportunity-zone-program).

The nomination is not the same as a final federal designation. Treasury still has to review and certify the tracts, and the state says that decision is expected later this fall. If the nominations are certified, the new zones will take effect Jan. 1, 2027, and remain in place through Dec. 31, 2036. Until that review is complete, communities and investors do not have a final map to rely on.

The scale is limited by the updated federal rules. Massachusetts had 414 eligible tracts to choose from but could nominate no more than 104, or roughly one-quarter of that pool. The state says the new eligibility standards are stricter than the rules used for the 2018 round, when 138 Massachusetts tracts were designated. A tract generally had to have a median family income at or below 70% of the area median, or a poverty rate of at least 20% combined with a median family income no higher than 125% of the area median. Contiguous tracts that might previously have been grouped together are no longer eligible under the updated rules, the state says.

The proposed map reaches several different parts of the Massachusetts economy. The state highlights innovation districts in Amherst, Boston, Cambridge, Lowell and Worcester, where universities and research institutions are tied to early-stage companies. It also points to working waterfronts from New Bedford to Gloucester, public-housing revitalization in Boston, and more than a dozen MBTA Communities districts, including Fall River, Framingham and Haverhill. In smaller Central and Western Massachusetts hubs, the state identifies Athol, Gardner, Greenfield, Montague, North Adams and Southbridge as places where mixed-use development could benefit from the designation.

Opportunity Zones work through federal tax treatment rather than a direct state construction grant. The [U.S. Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/tax-policy/data-transparency/qualified-opportunity-zones) says taxpayers who make qualifying investments in designated census tracts through Qualified Opportunity Funds may be eligible for tax benefits under Section 1400Z-2 of the Internal Revenue Code. The state’s [frequently asked questions](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/frequently-asked-opportunity-zone-questions) likewise explains that a designation makes investments eligible for incentives but does not itself attract money or guarantee that a project will be built. Communities still have to market sites, align zoning and permitting, and persuade investors that a project can work.

The 2026 framework includes enhanced treatment for rural funds. The state says a Qualified Rural Opportunity Fund investing in rural Opportunity Zones can use a 50% substantial-improvement threshold, compared with 100% elsewhere, and can receive a 30% basis step-up after five years instead of the 10% step-up available to other funds. Those provisions are intended to account for the different financing conditions in rural areas, but they do not predict how much capital will reach any particular town.

The immediate next step is federal certification, followed by local and private-sector decisions about which sites are ready for investment. Massachusetts says its selection process considered project readiness, local support, zoning and other public investments, but the nomination page does not promise a dollar amount, construction schedule or job total for any municipality. The practical test will come after the map is final: whether the tax incentive helps produce or preserve housing, strengthen small-city and rural economies, and move long-planned projects from eligibility to construction.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoDescription: Massachusetts nominated 104 census tracts across 46 municipalities for federal Opportunity Zone designation beginning in 2027, pending Treasury review.
